themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Five complaints of illegal tree damage were filed THIS WEEK in Central Harlem, a 344% spike from the 1.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, signaling potential organized or negligent destruction of street trees during spring season.
evidence: 5 illegal tree damage complaints filed this week vs. 1.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 4.96 indicates statistically significant deviation
Spike coincides with spring planting/renovation season
reporting_angles: Are contractors conducting unpermitted work on private properties and damaging city trees?
Investigate whether developers working on active ULURP projects (254 W 124th, One45 for Harlem, 2395 Frederick Douglass Blvd) are causing collateral damage to street tree canopy

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints nearly tripled THIS WEEK to 28 complaints, a 207% spike from the 9.1 weekly average over 8 weeks, potentially indicating increased traffic congestion, illegal street racing, or unmuffled commercial vehicles in Central Harlem.
evidence: 28 vehicle noise complaints this week vs. 9.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Part of broader noise complaint pattern (3,202 residential noise complaints over 90 days, highest category)
reporting_angles: Interview residents on high-traffic corridors (Frederick Douglass Blvd, 125th St, Amsterdam Ave) about spike in late-night street racing or delivery trucks
Request NYPD traffic enforcement data to see if complaint spike correlates with reduced enforcement or specific incidents this week

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Crisis Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints spiked to 3 filings LAST WEEK, a 500% jump from the 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks, mirroring the broader heat/hot water emergency (4,166 complaints in 90 days) and suggesting systemic building infrastructure failure across Central Harlem.
evidence: 3 plumbing complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Heat/hot water complaints (4,166 over 90 days) dominate the 311 dataset, suggesting infrastructure-wide failures in aging buildings
reporting_angles: Investigate whether this is NYCHA building degradation or private landlord neglect; cross-reference with NYC housing violation records
Interview residents about habitability; connect to broader City Limits story on East Harlem elevator/facility repairs and housing neglect
Request DOB data on recent DOE capital requests for building upgrades and plumbing infrastructure—is the city keeping pace with repairs?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity and Public Disorder Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 5 filings LAST WEEK, a 344% spike from the 1.1 weekly average over 8 weeks, coupled with a related 2300% spike in drinking-related complaints 3 weeks ago, indicating emerging open-air substance use and disorder in Central Harlem.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (8-week baseline), z-score 4.18
Drinking complaints spiked to 3 filings 3 weeks ago (2300% above 0.1 baseline, z-score 8.69)
Community board budget has repeatedly requested upgrades to homeless services facilities—suggests unmet need for substance use and housing services
reporting_angles: Identify neighborhood hotspots from 311 data; conduct street-level reporting on which blocks are experiencing open-air substance use
Interview NYPD about enforcement strategy and relationship to recent public safety data; ask about 'broken windows' vs. health-based responses
Connect to city's homelessness and substance abuse strategy—are new housing/treatment resources being deployed to Central Harlem?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk and Street Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 19 LAST WEEK, a 246% jump from the 5.5 weekly average, paired with a 1100% spike in litter basket requests last week, indicating rapid degradation of street infrastructure and sanitation in Central Harlem.
evidence: 19 sidewalk condition complaints last week vs. 5.5 weekly average (8-week baseline), z-score 7.49
3 litter basket requests last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (8-week baseline), 1100% spike with z-score 6.35
DOE has filed repeated capital budget requests for maintenance equipment, suggesting inadequate sanitation/infrastructure resources
reporting_angles: Walk major commercial corridors (125th St, Frederick Douglass Blvd, Amsterdam Ave) to document sidewalk damage, potholes, and lack of waste infrastructure
Analyze if this correlates with reduced street sweeping/sanitation worker allocation—request DSNY staffing and budget data for Central Harlem
Interview community board or district manager about unmet capital requests for street repair and maintenance equipment
